# heading-increment

- ID: `MD001`
- Category: Headings
- Default: on, severity warning
- Fixable: no
- Tags: `headings`

Each heading is at most one level deeper than the heading or title before it.

## Why

Headings form the outline of a document. A skipped level confuses readers,
especially people who use a screen reader to move between headings.

## Options

Set them under `rules.heading-increment.options`.

- `front_matter_title` (`string|false`, default `^\s*"?title"?\s*[:=]`): Regular
  expression, matched in any case, for the front matter line that gives the
  document a title, which counts as the top-level heading, so the first heading
  may be a level 2 heading. An empty string or false turns this off.

## Fix

There is no automatic fix. Only the author knows which level was meant.

## Example

This document breaks the rule:

```markdown
# Release notes

### Fixed

The parser keeps the spaces at the end of a line.
```

gomdlint reports:

```text
3:1 Heading level jumped from H1 to H3
```

This document follows the rule:

```markdown
# Release notes

## Fixed

The parser keeps the spaces at the end of a line.
```

## Configure

```yaml
rules:
  heading-increment:
    options:
      front_matter_title: ^\s*"?title"?\s*[:=]
```

Under `rules`, `heading-increment: false` turns the rule off and
`heading-increment: error` reports its findings as errors. The flag
`--disable heading-increment` turns it off for one run.

## Silence one line

```markdown
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line heading-increment -->
```
